what: One set of photo strips flows by itself at 40px per second. When you scroll down it turns to the opposite direction (the flow direction follows by .25 per frame so the turn is smooth) and speed is added by the scrolled distance (max 50). The added speed decays by multiplying .9 each frame, and the position chases its target by .2 so some inertia remains. When scrolling stops it keeps flowing slowly in the last direction. One set is attached before and after, so it loops endlessly.

options.speed: Base flow strength — speed×10 px per second, default 4
options.friction: Multiplier applied each frame to the speed gained from scroll, default .9
options.max: Max speed for scroll catch-up, default 50
options.lerp: Portion by which the position follows the target, default .2
options.turn: Share by which flow direction follows scroll direction, default .25 — at 0 it never turns around
options.strength: Multiplier that converts scroll distance into speed, default 1
options.dir: Initial flow direction — right (default, original) or left
options.invert: If false, it flows in the same direction when scrolling down (default is the opposite direction)
options.[data-fx-part=set]: The set to repeat (first child of the track) — the part duplicates it into two sets (data-fx-part=clone) is attached

from.where: index.html .ix-sep__slide (photo collection over the mountain band — original ScrollSynchroSlider speed 4 · velocityFriction .9 · maxV 50 · interpolation .2 · baseDirLerp .25 · delta 10×min(dt,.06), invertScrollDirection)

note: velocity-flip-marquee changes the timeline speed (speed cap 3, .3s), so its inertia and feel differ from this one, which adds px speed and settles with friction — that is why it was split out separately
